items.title: Irwin Leclere Interview, 1970-04-14
items.q: And then got in the audible in 1912... with Guy McCormick and a fellow by the name of Fitzgerald... And we played the off-room circuit.

ctx.x: And I wanted to ask you some things about your piano playing and composing. How did you get started?

Well, it's a strange thing. I used to have, my mother raised her niece years ago and she played a little piano. And I used to fool around watching her, you know. And I finally got to it and I played chopsticks, you know, those little things. I used to have to play with my mother. But it was the strangest thing in the world. When I learned how to play piano, it was a fellow, I can't think of his name. But I think it was Maple Leaf Rag or something like that. He taught me. And gee, that's the most difficult thing…
Yeah, well, I'll refresh your memory. Okay, a little bit. Did you ever get any piano teaching at all?
